To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the release of carbamezapine from the matrix granules and tablets can be controlled by the lipophilic and hydrophilic matrix components.
the release rate of carbamazepene (CBZ) from the granules and tablets can be controlled by varying the concentration of hydroxypropyl methyl cellulose (HPMC) and Avicel®.
the release mechanism from the matrix tablets follows non-Fickion diffusion shifting to case-II by the increase of the HPMC content.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of controlled-release CBZ tablets and granules by wet granulation and compression.

the effect of hydrophilic and lipophilic components on the release of CBZ from granules and tablets and the results indicate the possibility of achieving sustained release of CBZ using a combination of HPMC and Compritol® 88 ATO.
the effect of lipids and hydrophilic excipients on the release of CBZ from granules and tablets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lipophilic component (Compritol) is more effective than the hydrophilic one (HPMC) in controlling the release of carbazepine from matrix granules and tablets.
lipophilic and hydrophilic matrices could be used to formulate controlled-release CBZ tablets.

the lipophilic component (Compritol 888 ATO), hydrophilic component (Avicel PH102) and the concentration of HPMCAS are the most important factors for the release of carbamzepine from the granules and tablets and that wet granulation and compression is suitable method for preparation of controlled-release carbamazepine granules and tablets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the release mechanism of CBAZ from matrix tablet formulations was found to depend on both the drug loading and HPMC content.

the release mechanism is controlled by the hydrophilic component and the drug release from the granules and tablets is controlled by the diffusion of the drug through the matrix and erosion of the matrix.

the lipophilic component (Compritol 888ATO) plays a dominant role in the initial release of CBZ from granules and tablets, whereas the hydrophilic component (Avicel PH 101, HPMC) plays a major role for the later release of CBZ.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of lipophilic and hydrophilic matrix components can be a promising approach for the preparation of carbamazepin controlled-release granules and tablets.
the use of a lipophilic component in combination with a hydrophilic matrix component is a promising way for the formulation of sustained release tablets.
the release of carbamezepine from matrix tablets could be controlled by the amount of hydrophilic matrix components and the drug loading.
